why_no_signal.text: The header Export is one ExportButton built in index.tsx from a target the ACTIVE tab publishes upward. Performance publishes through ReportingTab's onExportTarget effect (told to index.tsx via TabShell's onReportingExportTarget into performanceExportTarget state); the target is built from the report's own retained_ref (report_id, revision), and is null when the report is not answer-bearing. Holdings has no export kind. AnalysisTab supplies none: it has no onExportTarget-shaped prop, TabShell mounts it without one, index.tsx has no state for one and hard-codes the Analysis gate closed (analysisExportGateOk = false), and its own comment says only that the header's Export 'targets this tab'. The reason a prop alone cannot be added: an Analysis export needs the retained Analysis report's id, revision and sha256, because the server resolves exactly one retained report by authorized_report_revisions[0].report_id and .revision and pins it as analysis_report_ref. No Analysis response served to the browser carries that identity: the Analysis wire and the owned-history slice carry request_id and attempt_id only, while the Performance wire carries retained_ref. Without an override index.tsx would name the client scope revision as the report ref, which is not a retained report id. Deriving one on the page, or sending the request id as report_id, would invent a payload.

other_tabs_export_target.performance: ReportingTab publishes via onExportTarget (ReportingTab.tsx:783-793; target built from report.retainedReport at :268-277 or from the dashboard series at :785-786); TabShell passes onReportingExportTarget through at TabShell.tsx:160; index.tsx stores it at :216 and reads it only on the reporting tab at :293 and :299; the Export props come from it at :316-332.
other_tabs_export_target.holdings: none: EXPORT_KIND_BY_TAB maps holdings to null (index.tsx:66), so the header shows the disabled control.

what_is_missing: A served member on the Analysis report response for the request being shown: the retained Analysis report's report_id, revision and sha256 with report_kind ANALYSIS (the shape Performance already serves as retained_ref). The CTO rules which route returns it and which of the tab's report sources Export follows.
not_established: Whether the producer already holds an Analysis retained report id that a route could return; no producer handler returns one today. Whether a live Analysis export through the current ExportButton is refused by the server was not exercised (no AWS call, no dev server).
